issues.label: Appealability/mandate posture
issues.why: The court must confirm the proper procedural vehicle and standard of review for challenging a stay order via writ of mandate.

issues.label: Authority to stay proceedings
issues.why: The court must identify the legal basis and limits of a California court’s power to stay an action in favor of another forum.

issues.label: Enforceability of bylaw forum clause
issues.why: The court must decide whether a forum-selection bylaw is valid and enforceable against a shareholder in these circumstances.

issues.label: Shareholder assent to bylaws
issues.why: The court must determine whether and how Salamon is bound by bylaws (including later-adopted amendments) as a shareholder.

issues.label: Clause mandatory vs permissive
issues.why: The court must construe whether the clause is exclusive/mandatory or merely permissive (the parties’ concession may not be dispositive).

issues.label: Scope of clause language
issues.why: The court must interpret whether an inspection-demand writ petition is an “action asserting a claim… governed by the internal affairs doctrine.”

issues.label: Internal affairs characterization
issues.why: The court must decide whether shareholder inspection rights are an internal corporate affair for a Delaware corporation operating in California.

issues.label: Choice of law for clause meaning
issues.why: The court must decide whether Delaware or California law governs interpretation of the bylaw forum-selection provision.

issues.label: Choice-of-law methodology
issues.why: The court must apply California choice-of-law rules (and any internal-affairs principles) to pick the governing interpretive law.

issues.label: Delaware law on inspections
issues.why: If Delaware law applies, the court must evaluate Delaware’s treatment of inspection demands as internal affairs and within such clauses.

issues.label: California law on inspections/internal affairs
issues.why: If California law applies, the court must evaluate California precedent on whether inspection demands implicate internal affairs for foreign corporations.

issues.label: California Corp Code 1600 applicability
issues.why: The court must decide whether section 1600’s shareholder-list right extends to a Delaware corporation with a principal office in California.

issues.label: California Corp Code 1601 applicability
issues.why: The court must decide whether section 1601 applies to this entity (e.g., “domestic corporation” text) and/or to foreign corporations in California.

issues.label: Section 2115 relevance
issues.why: The court must consider whether Corporations Code section 2115 (quasi-foreign corporation rules) affects inspection rights or internal-affairs analysis.

issues.label: Statutory prerequisites met
issues.why: The court must verify Salamon meets statutory thresholds (e.g., ≥5% voting shares) and any demand formalities under 1600/1601.

issues.label: Proper purpose under 1601
issues.why: For 1601 records, the court must determine whether Salamon’s stated purposes are reasonably related to his shareholder interests.

issues.label: Absolute right under 1600
issues.why: For 1600 shareholder lists, the court must address the “absolute” nature of the right and any permissible limitations (time, manner, misuse).

issues.label: Improper purpose defenses
issues.why: The court must consider Orchid’s claim that the demand is extortionate or pretextual and whether that limits inspection under CA/DE law.

issues.label: Overbreadth and tailoring
issues.why: The court must decide whether the request is overly broad (e.g., communications, gambling complaints) and whether any relief must be narrowed.

issues.label: Confidentiality and protective orders
issues.why: The court must consider whether sensitive financial/token/business data warrants confidentiality restrictions rather than outright denial/stay.

issues.label: Token (OXT) accounting relevance
issues.why: The court must determine whether cryptocurrency/token-treasury records are “books and records” subject to inspection and whether they’re reasonably related to valuation.

issues.label: Minutes/board materials scope
issues.why: The court must determine whether and to what extent board/committee minutes and related materials are inspectable under applicable law.

issues.label: Tax returns inspection limits
issues.why: The court must address whether corporate tax returns are within statutory inspection rights and any heightened need/limitations.

issues.label: Audit/financial statements obligations
issues.why: The court must consider whether failure to provide routine financials affects entitlement, urgency, or equitable considerations.

issues.label: Bylaw cannot waive statutory rights
issues.why: The court must assess whether a forum-selection bylaw effectively limits unwaivable statutory inspection rights under 1600(d)/1601(b).

issues.label: Public policy exception to enforcement
issues.why: The court must decide whether enforcing the forum clause contravenes a strong California public policy favoring shareholder inspection access.

issues.label: Adequacy of Delaware remedy
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether Delaware DGCL 220 provides a meaningful alternative remedy or would materially diminish Salamon’s protections.

issues.label: Comparative breadth CA vs DE
issues.why: The court must compare the scope/standards (absolute vs proper purpose; categories of records; burden of proof) to assess claimed deprivation.

issues.label: Unconscionability/reasonableness
issues.why: The court must consider whether enforcement would be unreasonable, unjust, or effectively deprive Salamon of his day in court.

issues.label: Forum clause notice/fairness
issues.why: The court must consider whether Salamon had notice of the bylaw forum clause and whether it was adopted/used inequitably.

issues.label: Application to non-Delaware resident
issues.why: The court must consider enforceability against a California resident shareholder and any due process constraints.

issues.label: Anti-suit/first-filed considerations
issues.why: The court must assess whether comity or first-to-file principles support a stay given the competing Delaware action.

issues.label: Effect of Delaware dismissal
issues.why: The court must account for the Delaware Court of Chancery’s dismissal for lack of personal jurisdiction and its impact on the rationale for a stay.

issues.label: Mootness of stay request
issues.why: If the Delaware action cannot proceed against Salamon, the court must decide whether there remains a proceeding to await, making the stay improper.

issues.label: Alternative Delaware forum availability
issues.why: The court must consider whether Orchid can refile in Delaware with jurisdiction (e.g., against the shares, via consent, or other mechanisms) and whether that is realistic.

issues.label: Personal jurisdiction realities
issues.why: The court must consider whether requiring Delaware litigation is feasible when Delaware courts lack personal jurisdiction over Salamon absent consent.

issues.label: Waiver by Orchid
issues.why: The court must consider whether Orchid waived or forfeited the forum clause by litigating in California or taking positions inconsistent with enforcement.

issues.label: Estoppel/judicial admissions
issues.why: The court must consider whether either party is estopped by prior representations (e.g., about governing law, clause scope, or Delaware action positions).

issues.label: Standard for granting stay
issues.why: The court must apply the correct legal standard for a stay based on a forum-selection clause (enforcement vs discretionary factors).

issues.label: Burden of proof on enforcement
issues.why: The court must allocate burdens (e.g., clause proponent shows applicability; opponent shows unreasonableness/public policy violation).

issues.label: Severability/partial enforcement
issues.why: The court must consider whether some claims (e.g., 1600 shareholder list) fall outside the clause even if others do, allowing partial stay.

issues.label: Relief framing under mandate
issues.why: The court must determine whether mandate is appropriate to compel inspection and whether there is a plain, speedy, adequate remedy at law.

issues.label: Timing/expedition needs
issues.why: The court must consider whether inspection rights require prompt adjudication and whether a stay would cause undue prejudice.

issues.label: Comity with Delaware courts
issues.why: The court must balance respect for Delaware’s interest in internal affairs against California’s regulatory interests for corporations operating here.

issues.label: Internal affairs doctrine limits
issues.why: The court must decide whether California can apply its inspection statutes to foreign corporations despite internal affairs doctrine exceptions.

issues.label: California constitutional/statutory policy
issues.why: The court must identify the strength and source of California’s policy supporting shareholder inspection and whether it is “fundamental.”

issues.label: Construction against drafter
issues.why: The court must consider interpretive canons for bylaws/contracts (ambiguities, corporate drafting) when construing clause scope.

issues.label: Definition of ‘claim against’
issues.why: The court must decide whether a writ petition to enforce statutory inspection rights is a “claim against the corporation” within the clause.

issues.label: Definition of ‘employee’ in clause
issues.why: The court must consider whether requested communications of board members implicate “director/officer/employee” language and coverage.

issues.label: Remedy if clause applies
issues.why: The court must decide whether proper remedy is dismissal, stay, or transfer, and under what conditions.

issues.label: Security/bond/costs issues
issues.why: The court must consider any statutory or equitable conditions on stay (e.g., costs, preservation of evidence, or undertaking).

issues.label: Preservation of records
issues.why: The court must consider whether to order preservation to prevent spoliation during a stay given the records sought.

issues.label: Judicial notice use/limits
issues.why: The court must ensure proper use of judicially noticed Delaware filings and whether they may be used for truth vs existence of proceedings.

issues.label: Issue preclusion from Delaware
issues.why: The court must consider whether the Delaware personal-jurisdiction ruling has preclusive effect on any California issues.

issues.label: Claim splitting/parallel actions
issues.why: The court must consider whether Salamon’s California petition and any Delaware 220 proceeding create duplicative litigation concerns.

issues.label: Standing and shareholder status
issues.why: The court must confirm Salamon’s current shareholder status and standing to demand inspection and seek mandamus.

issues.label: Subsidiary records access
issues.why: The court must decide whether inspection rights extend to subsidiary (Orchid Labs) books/records when demanded from parent Orchid.

issues.label: Gambling-law documents relevance
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether alleged illegality/mismanagement investigations justify access to complaint/communication documents under the governing statute.

issues.label: Attorney-client privilege
issues.why: The court must consider privilege limits on board communications and complaints, and whether any inspection can reach privileged material.

issues.label: Work-product doctrine
issues.why: The court must consider whether litigation-related materials (complaints/investigations) are protected from inspection.

issues.label: Trade secret protection
issues.why: The court must consider whether trade secret status limits inspection or requires protective conditions.

issues.label: Data privacy and third parties
issues.why: The court must consider privacy of employees/users/shareholders in requested records (names/addresses; complaints) and any redaction duties.
